To exploit the cross-sectional momentum strategy in the Indian equity market, we focus on identifying stocks that have historically outperformed their peers over a specific lookback period. The economic mechanism involves leveraging the tendency for strong performers to continue outperforming due to factors such as positive news flow, investor sentiment, and company-specific events. This persistence might persist because strong performance can attract further investment, compounding returns.

The strategy would involve ranking all stocks based on their recent returns over a 6-12 month period. The top decile of performers would be selected for long positions, while the bottom decile would be shorted. Weighing factors could include market capitalization and liquidity to ensure robust trading. This approach aims to capture the residual alpha generated by momentum effects across the Indian equity universe.

The signal for this strategy is computed using the stock returns over a 6-12 month lookback period. Specifically, we calculate the average monthly return for each stock during this timeframe. On any given day, all stocks in the Indian equity market are ranked based on these average returns. The top decile of stocks with the highest average returns over the past 6-12 months are selected for long positions, while the bottom decile with the lowest average returns are shorted. This ranking ensures that we identify the most persistently outperforming and underperforming stocks, leveraging the momentum effect in the market.

The strategy holds positions in 20% of the top decile (top 20 stocks) and 20% of the bottom decile (bottom 20 stocks), ensuring a balanced exposure. Long positions are weighted equally at 1%, while short positions are also weighted equally at -1%. This results in a maximum net position size of ±20%. Risk limits are set to prevent losses exceeding 5% of the portfolio value in any given month, safeguarding against extreme market movements and ensuring sustainable performance over time.
